evaluations.case_note_analysis:
Checked in with Daisy on 10/19 and successfully completed First Shift Orientation on Friday 10/23/2026 at Columbia Center.

**Latest Case Note Updates:** [Update 11/19/2026 • Jenn Jeanquart]: Client Status & Transition Planning

Residential Transition: Client is preparing to transition from the halfway house to home confinement next week. Client expressed positive anticipation regarding this transition, noting that being back with his family will be easier than the halfway house environment.
Transportation & Logistics: Client resides in Lexington and currently lacks a valid driver's license (holds a learner's permit; mother will not permit him to drive). He noted that paying for daily Uber rides from Lexington is not financially viable. However, he has arranged a secondary, under-the-table job working for his mother's boyfriend (2:00 PM–6:00 PM or 8:00 PM) and confirmed his mother's boyfriend will provide daily transportation via tow truck.
Employment & Workplace Readiness

Upcoming Interview: Client has a scheduled phone interview tomorrow at 12:30 PM with Charter Next Generation (cnginc.com) in Blythewood, a specialty film and sustainable material manufacturing plant.
Compensation & Shift Preferences: The position starts at $18.00/hour, with an additional $2.50/hour shift differential for overnight work. Client intends to pursue the overnight shift. He also discussed a potential opportunity at Sysco ($29.00/hour).
Workplace Boundaries & Retention Risks: Client expressed strong confidence in his work ethic and respectful demeanor, but stated a strict zero-tolerance boundary regarding supervisor communication. Specifically, client stated he will immediately walk off the job—regardless of pay—if a supervisor uses profanity or specific derogatory language (e.g., "the B-word") toward him. Case manager explored alternative conflict-resolution strategies (e.g., speaking with the supervisor privately or escalating to HR), which the client declined, maintaining that walking away is his firm boundary.
Mental Health & Coping

Emotional Regulation: Client identified managing his "mental" health as his biggest challenge over the past week, citing cumulative grief from past losses. He described experiencing periods of emotional shutdown where he feels unable to speak or open up, noting a long-standing habit of bottling up his feelings and avoiding personal stressors by focusing on others or "running" from difficult emotions.
Coping Mechanisms: When feeling overwhelmed or shut down, client utilizes sleep to reset. Despite experiencing difficult mental health days while in the program, client has consistently shown up and met all program expectations.
Action Plan & Follow-Up

Client: Complete the 12:30 PM phone interview with Charter Next Generation tomorrow and update the case manager on the outcome.
Case Manager: Available to assist client with interview preparation and practice questions prior to tomorrow's call. | [Update 11/10/2026 • Jenn Jeanquart]: 1. Purpose of Contact
To review client's progress in the Turn90 program, calculate outstanding fines/fees for driver’s license reinstatement, and assess current employment opportunities and scheduling.

2. Driver’s License Reinstatement Plan
Verification & Fee Breakdown: Case Manager and client reviewed the client's DMV records and tickets. Total outstanding ticket fines equal $550 across three citations ($155, $155, and $232).
Payment Agreement:
The client agreed to begin paying off the tickets in installments, starting with the first $155 payment next week.
Case Manager confirmed program assistance: once the client pays the initial tickets and is ready to make the final payment, the program will cover the DMV reinstatement fees so the client can regain his license.
3. Employment & Program Participation
Job Offer Evaluation: The client discussed an external job opportunity paying roughly $600/week. After running a cost-benefit analysis (accounting for transportation/Uber expenses of ~$150/week and meals), the client determined the net gain would only be around $300/week, making the trade-off impractical.
Turn90 Commitment:
The client has 5 weeks remaining in the Turn90 program.
Case Manager discussed program rules and waitlist constraints (12 individuals currently waiting), noting that taking an outside job now would lead to early discharge from the program.
The client expressed a strong desire to stay enrolled to complete the curriculum and personal development work.
Case Manager advised keeping staffing agency opportunities (e.g., Nova/Michelin, International Paper) as a structured backup plan for when Turn90 concludes.
Next Steps on Employment: Client decided not to attend the upcoming interview, and Case Manager coached the client on professional etiquette to call ahead and cancel respectfully rather than no-showing.
4. Behavioral Health & Cognitive Skills Application
CBT / Skill Utilization: Client reflected on how cognitive-behavioral tools learned in class (the "iceberg" concept, connecting thoughts, feelings, and actions) are helping him pause and think through situations rather than reacting impulsively. He noted increased patience and understanding of others' perspectives.
Court/Supervision Obligations: Client confirmed he is starting his first 52-week class session this week.
5. Action Items & Follow-Up
Client to contact the prospective employer/recruiter to formally cancel the interview.
Client to make the first ticket payment ($155) next week and retain proof of payment.
Client to attend first 52-week class session this week.
Case Manager will monitor client’s attendance/progress in Turn90 classes and coordinate reinstatement fee coverage once client nears ticket payoff. | [Update 11/03/2026 • Jenn Jeanquart]: ### 1. Data (Objective & Subjective Information)

* **Documentation & Vital Records:**
* Client reported that he forgot his DMV documentation at home but confirmed he will retrieve it tomorrow.
* Client verified that his physical REAL ID card has arrived and is currently in his possession (received via mail/delivered to his mother's address).
* Client confirmed an appointment scheduled for tomorrow at the Social Security Administration (SSA).
* Address on file/ID verified: Client provided address on *Colony Lake Drive, Lexington*. Client plans to stay with his mother upon transition from the halfway house (approx. 90-day mark).

* **Employment & Training Goals:**
* Client is scheduled for Forklift Training/Certification on Friday. Case Manager (CM) noted lunch will be provided and no equipment needs to be brought.
* Client expressed high interest in obtaining a night-shift forklift operator position so he can maintain regular daytime program participation/attendance.
* CM discussed an employment pathway via a staffing/temp agency (30–90 day trial to permanent placement) at the Michelin tire manufacturing facility in Lexington (approx. starting pay $18/hr, increasing to $20+/hr upon direct hire).
* CM and client agreed to begin formal job applications around Week 3 or 4 of the program.

* **Personal Goals & Budgeting:**
* Client stated an interest in purchasing a vehicle (TRX truck) in the future; however, he demonstrated sound sequencing by stating he intends to secure steady forklift employment and verify income stability before pursuing a vehicle purchase.

* **Mental Health & Emotional Well-Being:**
* When asked about recent difficulties, client disclosed experiencing internal mental/emotional stress ("crazy thoughts") that have persisted since age 14.
* Client expressed hesitation toward formal counseling, indicating he feels he must manage it independently and stating, "I'm just here for them [my family]... I don't care about me."
* CM validated client’s feelings, provided supportive reassurance, and established an open-door policy should client experience overwhelming days and wish to talk.

---

### 2. Assessment

* **Engagement & Demeanor:** Client presented as polite, cooperative, future-focused, and engaged ("Yes, ma'am" throughout). Maintained consistent eye contact and realistic goal orientation.
* **Re-entry Progress:** Client is making positive, proactive strides in Week 2, having secured his REAL ID and adhering to his SSA and forklift training schedules. He demonstrates practical impulse control regarding major financial decisions (deferring vehicle purchase until income is proven).
* **Risk Factors / Needs:** Client exhibits signs of self-neglect/avoidant coping regarding long-standing mental health struggles and a lack of self-prioritization. While he denies intent to harm himself ("I don't feel like I'll ever go through"), his dismissive attitude toward personal well-being warrants ongoing supportive monitoring and low-pressure engagement regarding counseling resources.

---

### 3. Plan & Next Steps

1. **Client Action Items:**
* Retrieve DMV paperwork and provide to CM tomorrow.
* Attend scheduled Social Security Administration appointment tomorrow.
* Attend and complete Forklift Certification course this Friday.

2. **Case Manager Action Items:**
* Confirm client attendance and completion of Friday's forklift certification.
* Follow up on SSA appointment outcome and DMV paper collection.
* Connect with staffing partner/temp agency contact regarding Michelin forklift night-shift opportunities ahead of Weeks 3–4 application timeline.
* Continue routine check-ins on client's emotional well-being; gently explore readiness for supportive wellness resources as rapport deepens. | [Update 10/29/2026 • Jenn Jeanquart]: Met for Initial Case Management Session. 

Briefcase & Gates Update:
- Gate 1 (IDs): Participant has his Birth Certificate. Needs a physical Social Security Card (plans to order online). Knows his state ID number by heart.
- Gate 2 (Housing/DL): Stays in Lexington. Owes ~$300 in reinstatement fees + potential ticket fees. Plans to pay these off in ~2 weeks to get a beginner's permit. Will use computer lab time to study for the permit test.
- Gate 3 (Health/Bank): Needs dental work (wisdom teeth) and an eye exam (glasses). Mother is assisting with insurance. Discussed setting up a traditional bank account (FCU/local bank) rather than Chime to assist with credit building.

CBT / Action Plan Alignment:

- Order SSN card online.
- Review ticket fees/reinstatement fees and plan for payment.
- Utilize computer lab for DMV permit practice tests.
